accident_report: V1 (Vehicle 1) is in Lane 2 (second lane from the right), 15 meters ahead of V2 (which is also in Lane 2), and intends to make a left turn. V2 (Vehicle 2) is in Lane 2, 15 meters behind V1, and is traveling in the same direction as V1. V3 (Vehicle 3) is in Lane 3 (third lane from the right), parallel to V2 and slightly behind V2. V1 is traveling in Lane 2 and signals its intention to make a left turn. V1 slows down and comes to a stop in Lane 2 because it needs to make a left turn across oncoming traffic. V2, which was initially following V1 in Lane 2, fails to notice that V1 has stopped because V2's driver is distracted by a phone call. V2 continues traveling at a high speed and does not slow down until it is too late, resulting in a rear-end collision where V2 collides with V1. V3, traveling in Lane 3, observes the collision and swerves slightly to the right to avoid any debris from the collision but manages to stay in Lane 3 and does not make contact with any other vehicle. The outcome is a rear-end collision where V2 collides with V1 while V1 is stopped in Lane 2 waiting to make a left turn. V3 avoids any direct collision but is affected by the incident.
